metadata.title: Resume Eligibility

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for determining whether a system may safely resume operation following disruption, recovery, or halt.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Resilience decision gating, restart authorization, execution suppression, and safe resumption control.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust pattern defining explicit eligibility criteria for resuming system operation.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines resume eligibility as trust-relevant resilience decision data.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Continuity and recovery controls (CP-3, CP-7, CP-8, CP-10) are constrained by resume eligibility.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance requiring explicit authorization before resumption of operation.

metadata.remarks: Resume Eligibility defines whether resumption of execution is permitted following disruption, restore, degradation, or halt. This pattern establishes non-equivalence between technical recovery and permission to operate.

components.title: Resume Eligibility Criteria
components.description: Defines required conditions that must be satisfied before resumption is permitted.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Resumption of operations is explicitly governed.

components.title: Resume Suppression
components.description: Prevents resumption when eligibility conditions are not met.

components.title: Explicit Resume Authorization
components.description: Requires explicit authorization signal before resuming execution.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Resilience governance defines who may approve resumption.

components.title: Resume Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what successful recovery or restoration does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Ability to recover does not imply permission to resume operations.

components.title: Resume Eligibility Signaling
components.description: Emission of explicit resume‑permitted or resume‑prohibited signals.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Alternate and suppressed operational states are visible.
